name: application-clause-accordion
title: Clause Accordion
description: Numbered legal-clause list where each clause has an expand/collapse header, a stable anchor link for deep-linking, and body text.
useWhen: Rendering Terms of Service, a Privacy Policy, or a contract broken into numbered clauses.
Users need to deep-link to a specific clause (e.g. from a footnote or support reference) via a stable anchor.
Distinct from the generic Accordions component in its numbering convention and per-clause copy-link affordance, both specific to legal documents.
avoidWhen: The content isn't numbered/clause-structured — use the generic Accordions component instead.
You need all sections visible simultaneously for printing or review — a flat numbered list without collapse may serve better.
responsiveBehavior: Each clause header is a single row with the number, title, link icon, and chevron; the title wraps rather than truncating so full clause names stay readable.
accessibility: Each header button carries aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at its clause body's id, following the standard disclosure pattern.
The chevron rotates to reflect open/closed state, but the underlying aria-expanded value is the actual source of truth for assistive technology.

The anchor link uses a real href ("#clause-id") so it works even with JavaScript disabled or for right-click/copy-link, and carries an aria-label describing which clause it links to since its icon has no visible text.

variants.title: Clause Accordion
variants.description: Three numbered clauses (Acceptance of terms, User responsibilities, Limitation of liability), with the first expanded showing its body text and an anchor-link icon on each header.
accessibility: Each clause's anchor link is a real, right-clickable href, not a JavaScript-only copy action.

variants.title: Clause Accordion (Dark)
variants.description: The same three-clause list adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Number badge, chevron, and link-icon contrast remain legible against the dark surface.
